regime_context: The detector shows a defensive/healthcare leadership concentration: Big Pharma is the headline theme (eligible, durability 0.84, breadth 1.0, crowded), with Health Care EW, Defensives, and Consumer Staples EW all eligible, trend-tagged, high-durability, and crowded. Rotation breadth is narrowing (39% eligible) and absorption is low (0.32, not one-narrative), while the momentum leader is Memory/HBM/Storage but it is NOT eligible (gate blocks it). The gate_helps flag is true for this market, so the absolute-trend filter has historically cut drawdown. My own track record is directionally weak (dir_accuracy 0.413 over n=138), so I stay humble and lean low conviction.
emerging_watch: Watching whether the eligible defensive cluster (Big Pharma, Staples, Insurance) keeps breadth above ~0.8 while the ineligible AI/tech leaders (Memory/HBM, AI Semis) stay gated out — a confirmed handoff would be Memory/HBM regaining eligible=true while Big Pharma loses eligible=true; until that flips, the defensive leadership stands.

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the headline theme and the strongest eligible leader after the gate screen. It is trend-tagged, durability is high (0.84), breadth is 1.0 (every constituent participating), and it passes the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true). This is the one leg with validated drawdown control, so the conditional lean is to stay on the side of the trend as long as the gate holds. Crowding (z=1.46) is a size-down caution, not a contrary signal.
evidence: headline.id = big_pharma with durability_bar 0.84 and hurst_tag 'trend'
rank 2 overall but rank 1 among eligible themes
theses.dissent: Big Pharma is crowded and already the headline; attention spikes in thematic equities often mark local tops, and the detector explicitly warns not to treat attention/flow as a buy. A crowded defensive trade can unwind fast if rates or risk appetite turn.

falsifier.text: PPH closes below its 20-day low or the Big Pharma theme drops out of eligible=true before the check-by date

theses.subject: Consumer Staples (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Consumer Staples EW is eligible, trend-tagged, with durability 0.80 and breadth 0.879, sitting inside the same defensive leadership cluster as Big Pharma and Defensives. It passes the trend gate, which is the validated risk-control leg. Crowding (z=1.89) is the highest in the eligible defensive group, so this is a size-down lean, not a strong call.
theses.dissent: Staples is the most crowded defensive theme in the set; if the defensive trade reverses, the most crowded name is likely to give back the most. Low breadth relative to Big Pharma (0.879 vs 1.0) also suggests slightly weaker internal cohesion.

falsifier.text: XLP underperforms XLV by 3% or more over any 20-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Insurance & Brokers
theses.thesis: Insurance & Brokers is eligible, trend-mixed but durability 0.68, with high breadth (0.947) and crowded (z=1.67). It sits in the same eligible defensive/financial defensive cluster and passes the gate. The lean is only that it remains on the right side of the trend filter; crowding is again a size-down caution.
theses.dissent: Mixed hurst tag (not pure trend) and crowded; insurance can be rate-sensitive and the macro backdrop shows unscheduled surprise share at 1.0, meaning news-driven reversals are a live risk.

falsifier.text: KIE closes below its 50-day moving average and stays below for 5 consecutive sessions before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
